practicalRatings.low: Straightforward to operate at the table
practicalRatings.high: Tracks many choices, entities, timings or resources

practicalRatings.low: Functions mainly from one key ability
Core identity works with little specialised equipment
practicalRatings.high: Relies heavily on particular equipment and upgrades
Frequent management of several limited resources

practicalScale.rule: Use the middle value for a meaningful but non-defining burden or benefit; avoid false numeric precision.

enemySpecialization.purpose: Sparse mechanical aptitude against a requested kind of enemy. This is separate from spiritualThemes: commanding, becoming or studying a creature does not imply being especially effective against it.
enemySpecialization.omissionRule: An omitted target means no documented special advantage against it; do not populate every target with absent.

levels.available: The class or archetype can gain or already has a meaningful advantage against this target, but it is conditional, optional or secondary.
levels.core: The advantage is built in, broadly reliable against the target and central to the option's identity or performance.

matchingRules: Prefer an exact target match; a broader parent target remains a valid but less specific match.
user-chosen creature type can match any requested creature type, but the recommendation must disclose that the player must make or activate that choice.
Alignment-based abilities only support a creature target when they reliably apply to that target; otherwise use available and disclose the condition.
Never infer hunting aptitude from spiritualThemes or narrative theme alone.
enemySpecialization.evidenceRule: Every non-empty class assignment and every archetype override must identify the source feature that supports it.

professionIdentityRules: Assign only when the official name or source text explicitly presents the archetype as that profession or vocation.
Do not infer a profession from a skill rank, class skill or thematic resemblance alone.
Store the supporting source excerpt and source reference with every assigned profession value.
Allow multiple values when the source explicitly supports them.

constraintKinds.requirement: Determines whether the option can legally be selected.
constraintKinds.commitment: Does not normally block selection, but creates an ongoing behavioural, build or narrative obligation.
constraintKinds.theme: Describes identity without imposing a material mechanical restriction.
